translations.text: And at that time I told you, “I cannot bear the burden of you by myself.”
How can I bear your troubles, your conflicts, and your quarrels?
And they took some of the land’s fruit in their hands and brought it to us, saying to us, “The land that the Lord our God will give us is good.”

Where are we going up to? Your brothers discouraged you, saying, “We saw a great nation, numerous and stronger than we are, and great cities with walls built up to heaven. We also saw the descendants of the giants there.”
I spoke to you, but you did not listen to me. You disobeyed the Lord’s command, forced your way ahead, and went up the mountain.
For today you will pass through the territory of Moab, at Seir.
But God took you and brought you out of the iron furnace, which is the land of Egypt, to become his own people, as you are today.
And the Lord will scatter you among all the nations, and you will be left few in number among the nations into which the Lord God will bring you.
And there you will serve other gods, objects made by human hands from wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell.
And today you must understand and consider in your heart that the Lord your God is the one in heaven above and on the earth below. There is no other besides him.
Then Moses set apart three cities on the other side of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.
Moses called together all [?] and said to them, “Listen, Israel, to the statutes and judgments that I will speak in your hearing today, so that you may learn them and take care to carry them out.”

But the seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God. You must not do any work on it—you, your son, your daughter, your male slave, your female slave, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the foreign resident within your gates—so that your slave may rest just as you do.
You must not testify falsely against your neighbor by giving false testimony.
And when you heard the voice from the midst of the fire, while the mountain was ablaze, you came to me—the leaders of your tribes and your elders.

Instead, follow the whole path that the Lord your God has commanded you to walk, so that he may give you rest, things may go well for you, and you may live many days in the land that you will inherit.

So that you may fear the Lord our God, keeping all his statutes and commandments that I am giving you today—you, your children, and your children’s children, throughout all the days of their lives—and so that you may live many days.
And when the Lord your God brings you into the land concerning which the Lord your God swore to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you great and good cities that you did not build,
You must not give your daughter to his son, and you must not take his daughter for your son.
For she will turn your son away from me, and he will serve other gods. Then the Lord will become angry with you and quickly destroy you.
And he will hand their kings over to you, and you will erase their names from that place. No one will stand against you until you have destroyed them.
Therefore, you must not bring a detestable thing into your house, lest you too become detestable like it. You must utterly hate it and utterly detest it, because it is defiled.

And when the Lord your God wipes out all these nations before you, do not say in your heart, “It is because of my righteousness that the Lord has brought me in to inherit this good land.” Rather, it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the Lord will destroy them before you.
And when I saw that you had sinned before the Lord your God, and had made yourselves a cast-metal god, and had abandoned the way that the Lord had commanded you to follow,
The Lord was also very angry with Aaron and intended to destroy him. And I also prayed for Aaron at that time.
You have been unfaithful to the Lord since the day he revealed himself to you.

And I prayed to God, saying, “Lord, Lord, king of the gods, do not destroy your people and your inheritance, whom you redeemed by your power, by your mighty hand, and by your uplifted arm, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt.”
Look, heaven belongs to the Lord your God, as do the heaven of heavens and the earth, with everything in them.
Fear the Lord your God, serve him alone, hold fast to him, and swear by his name.
And you shall love the Lord your God and keep his instructions, which he commanded you, and his statutes, his commandments, and his judgments, throughout all your days.
But if you obey all these commandments that I am commanding you today, carrying them out, loving the Lord our God, walking in all his commandments, and holding fast to him,
Then the Lord will drive out all these nations before you, and you will take possession of great nations much stronger than you.
You must not do these things to the Lord your God.
And bring there your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your firstfruits, your tithes, your vowed offerings, and the firstborn of your cattle and sheep.
But when the Lord your God destroys all the nations whose land you are entering to possess, and you take possession of them and settle in their land,
You must not do these things to the Lord your God, for they have done for their gods the abominations that the Lord hates. They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire for their gods.
You must not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer, for the Lord your God is testing you to reveal whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
From among the gods of the nations around you, those near you and those far from you, from one end of the earth to the other.
You may eat every clean bird.
And the vulture and the [?], and those like them.
You shall freely open your hand to him and lend him whatever he needs, according to his lack.

Instead, you shall freely give to him and freely lend him whatever he needs. Your heart must not be grieved when you give to him, because on account of this the Lord your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you undertake.
And you shall boil it, roast it, and eat it in the place that the Lord your God will choose. In the morning you shall turn back and go to your own place.

You shall take care to administer justice truthfully, so that you may live and enter and take possession of the land that the Lord your God will give you, tribe by tribe. And they shall judge the people with just judgment.
You must not slaughter for the Lord your God an ox or a sheep that has a defect. Every evil thing is an abomination to the Lord your God.
You shall bring out that man or that woman, and they shall stone them to death.
It shall remain with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord your God and keep all these commandments and statutes by carrying them out.
No one who [?] shall be found among you, purifying his son or daughter in fire, practicing divination, interpreting omens, observing signs, practicing sorcery, or casting spells.
The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers, and you must listen to him.

Prepare the road for yourself, and divide the territory of your land into three parts—the land that the Lord your God will allot to you—so that they may be places of refuge for anyone who kills someone.
And if you do not want her, you must send her away free. You must not sell her for money, and you must not mistreat her, because you have humiliated her.
And on the day when he gives his possessions to his sons as an inheritance, he must not make the son of the loved woman the firstborn, overlooking the son of the hated woman, who is the firstborn.
But if someone has a disobedient son who defies him and does not listen to his father and mother, and who still does not listen to them when they discipline him, his father and mother must seize him.
But if this accusation is true, and no evidence of the young woman's virginity is found,
you must do nothing to the young woman. She has committed no sin deserving death, because this case is like that of a man who attacks his neighbor and kills him.
A man whose genitals are crushed or cut off must not enter the assembly of the Lord.
You must never speak to them of peace or of what benefits them, for all time.
You must not bring a prostitute's earnings or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord your God in fulfillment of any vow, because these are detestable to the Lord your God.
But if a man is caught kidnapping someone from among his brothers, the children of [?], and overpowering him and selling him, that thief must die. You must remove the evil person from among you.
But if a dispute arises between people and they come for judgment, they must be judged: the wicked person must be condemned, and the righteous person acquitted.

When you have finished giving the entire tithe of your land's produce in the third year, you must give the second tithe to the Levite, the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow, so that they may eat in your towns and be satisfied.

Look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless your people [?] and the land you have given them, just as you swore to our ancestors that you would give us a land flowing with milk and honey.
And on the day when you cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord your God will give you, you must set up these two large stones and coat them with plaster.
Write on the stones all the words of this law when you cross the Jordan to enter the land flowing with milk and honey, just as the Lord, the God of your ancestors, told you.
And offer a sacrifice of well-being there to the Lord your God. Eat there and be satisfied, and rejoice before the Lord your God.
Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his father's sister. And all the people shall say, “So be it.”
Cursed is anyone who accepts a bribe to kill someone and shed innocent blood. And all the people shall say, “So be it.”
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head over you, but you will be like a tail.
And they will be signs and wonders among you and among your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a glad heart because of the abundance of all you had produced,

you will eat the flesh of the offspring of your womb [?], your sons and daughters whom the Lord gave you. You will eat them during your siege and in the distress with which the enemy will oppress you.
And he will bring back upon you all the terrible suffering of Egypt that you feared, and these troubles will come upon you.
But also with the others who are here with you today before the Lord your God, and with the others who are not here with you today.
For you know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the nations through which you passed.
And the Lord will set [?] apart for disaster from among all the children of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant written in the book of this law.

And Moses called Joshua and said to him in the presence of all [?], “Be strong and stand firm, for you are the one who will lead this people into the land that the Lord swore to our ancestors to give them, and you are the one who will divide it up as an inheritance.”

For I will bring them into the good land that I swore to their ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey. They will eat and be satisfied and prosper, and they will turn to foreign gods and serve them. They will provoke me and break my covenant.
For I have proclaimed the name of the Lord. Ascribe greatness to our God.
See, see that I am he, and there is no other god besides me. I am the one who will kill and give life. I will strike, and I will also heal, and no one can rescue anyone from my hands.
Moses was 120 years old when he died, and his eyes had neither grown dim nor failed.
And Joshua son of Nun was filled with wisdom, for Moses had laid his hand on him. The children of [?] obeyed him and did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
